# === Syntax ===

--8<-- [start:throw_1]
throw(error(type_error(integer, foo), context))
--8<-- [end:throw_1]

--8<-- [start:catch_2]
catch(Goal, ERROR)
--8<-- [end:catch_2]

--8<-- [start:catch_2_ex2]
# Catch any exception
catch(Goal, ERROR)

# Catch a specific Python exception by class
catch(++(some_python_call()), ++ValueError(MSG))

# Catch a structured logic error
catch(Goal, error(type_error(_, _), _))
--8<-- [end:catch_2_ex2]

--8<-- [start:catch_recover_3]
catch_recover(Goal, ERROR, Recovery)
--8<-- [end:catch_recover_3]

--8<-- [start:catch_3]
catch(
    ++(some_python_call()),
    ++ValueError(MSG),
    handle_error(MSG)
)
--8<-- [end:catch_3]


# === Unified Exception Representation ===

--8<-- [start:unified_exception_representation]
# Logic exception: throw(my_error(42))  →  ERROR = my_error(42)
# Python exception: ValueError("bad")  →  ERROR = ValueError("bad")

catch(Goal, ERROR)          # always catches, binds ERROR
catch_recover(Goal, ERROR, Recovery)  # catches, binds ERROR, runs Recovery
catch(Goal, my_error(N), Recovery)   # selective: re-raises if no match
--8<-- [end:unified_exception_representation]

# === Additional (indented blocks) ===

--8<-- [start:logicexception]
check_int(X, R) <- catch(
    (X > 0, R is "positive"),
    error(type_error(_, _), _),
    R is "not a number"
)
--8<-- [end:logicexception]

--8<-- [start:logicexception_ex2]
safe_parse(S, R) <- (
    catch(++(int(S)), ++ValueError(_)),
    R is "parse error"
)
--8<-- [end:logicexception_ex2]

--8<-- [start:logicexception_ex3]
logged_op(X, Y, R) <- catch_recover(
    (R == X / Y),
    ERR,
    (write_text(ERR), R is "error")
)
--8<-- [end:logicexception_ex3]

--8<-- [start:logicexception_ex4]
logged_div(X, Y, R) <- catch(
    (R == X / Y),
    E,
    (write_text(E), throw(E))
)
--8<-- [end:logicexception_ex4]

--8<-- [start:logicexception_ex5]
safe_run(GOAL, R) <- (
    catch(call_goal(GOAL), _),
    R is "ok"
)
--8<-- [end:logicexception_ex5]
